title: One app.mojo, every screen, agent tools built in
subtitle: The same view() and update() become native screens and an MCP tool server

nodes.label: Linux
nodes.desc: Runs today. Every check in the repo drives the app here on a headless display.

nodes.label: Mac
nodes.desc: Runs on GitHub's macOS runners (scripts/mac-ci); omxplorer ships as a Mac app with its queries on Metal.

nodes.label: Web
nodes.desc: Runs today: the web host draws real HTML from the app. Next: the GPU work in the browser through WebGPU.

nodes.label: Android
nodes.desc: Runs on the Android emulator with Android's own views. Phones are on the roadmap.

nodes.label: iPhone
nodes.desc: Builds and signs. Running it on a phone is on the roadmap.

nodes.label: Agent tools
nodes.desc: Every app is an MCP tool server: a button becomes a tool, a field a tool with text. A disabled button is not a tool.

nodes.label: Agent screens
nodes.desc: An agent answers with UI as data; it is checked against the component catalog, then drawn natively.

nodes.label: app.mojo
nodes.desc: Two functions. view() describes the screen; update() reacts to a tap, a key or an agent's call. One way to do each thing.

nodes.label: Jobs
nodes.desc: Slow work (a query, a video decode, OCR) runs on its own thread; its answer comes back to update() as an event.

nodes.label: Data engine
nodes.desc: Tables, SQL and group-bys over millions of rows, in the app's own process; videos and documents become tables too, linked by key, time or place.

nodes.label: GPU
nodes.desc: The same language as the buttons: Mojo kernels on NVIDIA (CUDA-class) and Apple (Metal).

flows.name: A tap
flows.desc: A person taps a button on any screen.

steps.note: The tap reaches update() as an event, the same on every platform.
update() asks the data engine for the new numbers, in the same process: no HTTP, no JSON.
The group-by runs as a Mojo kernel on the GPU.
The answer stays in the app's memory.
The host updates only what changed, with its own native widgets.

flows.name: An agent calls a button
flows.desc: An agent uses the same app through MCP.

steps.note: The agent calls a tool; to the app it is the same event as a tap.
update() runs exactly as it would for a person.
The reply says what changed in words: new texts, what opened, which tools appeared.
